prompt:
Pixel art for a 16-bit style side-view arena shooter that runs at 640x360. Edit the attached template in place: it is drawn on a chunky pixel grid where one art pixel is exactly 1/240 of the image width; keep exactly that pixel size (never finer, never subdivided), and keep every size anchor and guide position. Crisp hard pixels: a clean 1-pixel near-black outline around every character, Enemy and prop; flat cel shading with 3-4 tones per material, shadows leaning purple-blue and highlights leaning warm yellow, light from the upper left; no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no blur, no soft edges, no semi-transparent pixels (use a checkerboard dither for any in-between tone). Characters are seen in a three-quarter side view (Metal Slug style): facing right, head and chest turned slightly toward the viewer. No text, no watermark, no shadows on the ground unless asked.

Image 1 is the template to edit. On the far left stands Rexi, a 64-pixel-tall judge: he is only the size anchor, leave him exactly as he is. To his right are three light grey boxes, each holding a small rough draft of the same Enemy, the "Maletín-cóptero". Redraw the draft in every box as finished, detailed pixel art that fills its box: about 46 pixels wide and 28 pixels tall, never past the box edges, the three copies identical in design, side by side and not touching. Image 2 is the concept art for this Enemy (it faces right here too): follow its design, shapes and materials, but never its size. Keep exactly the template's pixel size.

The Maletín-cóptero, facing right: a brown leather briefcase turned into a small helicopter.
1) At the front (right end) a rounded glass bubble cockpit, light blue with a white glint, holding a tiny cartoon lawyer pilot seen in three-quarter view: slicked-back black hair, a cross frown, a white shirt collar, a red tie and a navy suit, both hands on a control stick.
2) The main body is a chunky briefcase, taller than in the draft: a front flap with a stitched seam, two brass clasps and a small brass lock, leather in four tones from a dark red-brown shadow to a warm tan highlight on the top edge.
3) On top, the briefcase's carrying handle; a short grey steel rotor mast rises from the handle to a small brass hub at the top. NO rotor blades and no rotor blur: the blades are animated in code.
4) At the back (left end) a tapered leather tail boom ending in a small brass hub for the tail rotor. NO tail-rotor blades.
5) Under the cockpit nose, a short dark steel gun barrel pointing right.
Plain white background, no muzzle flash, no motion lines, no shadow under it.
